# The MeshTransformer stack {#sec-mesh-attention}

This chapter describes the mesh-native operator layers as implemented in
`physicsnemo/experimental/nn/mesh_attention/` (`attention.py`, `block.py`,
`model.py`). The design goal is a **global, quadrature-aware,
O($D$)-equivariant primitive** with exact linear complexity in entity count —
and an honest statement of what such a primitive *cannot* represent.

The stack's lineage is explicit: it exists to **generalize GLOBE** (arXiv
[2511.15856](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.15856)), a boundary-element
surrogate for boundary-driven PDEs, carrying over its theoretical core while
replacing its bespoke machinery with mainstream transformer patterns. What
is kept: the equivariance structure of @sec-pde-theory — boundary-to-interior
propagation equivariant under the similarity group, with rotational symmetry
broken only by directional data on the boundary, so learned maps see only
joint invariants of relative displacement, normals, and boundary vector data
— together with all-to-all boundary-integral information flow under
quadrature weighting, and rigorous nondimensionalization. What is replaced:
GLOBE's Padé-approximant kernel MLPs, hand-assembled multiscale kernel
branches, and communication hyperlayers give way to standard attention
blocks, residual streams, and typed projections in the style of transformer
PDE surrogates such as Transolver (arXiv
[2402.02366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02366)) — trading special-purpose
kernel machinery for the simplicity and flexibility of mainstream-ML
components while keeping the contracts exact.

## Typed state: invariant scalars and polar vectors

All latent state lives in a `ScalarVectorState`: invariant scalar channels of
shape $(N, C_s)$ and polar-vector channels of shape $(N, C_v, D)$. Nothing
else is representable — pseudoscalars, axial vectors, and higher O($D$)
irreps are rejected rather than silently flattened into channels.

Equivariance is obtained **by construction** in `TypedProjection`:

- scalar outputs are a learned linear map of the input scalars *plus the
  Gram invariants* $v_a \cdot v_b$ of the vector channels;
- vector outputs mix vector *channels* only, with one coefficient per channel
  pair applied identically to every Cartesian component:
  $v^{\text{out}}_{o} = \sum_c W_{oc}\, v_c$.

No learned layer ever sees a raw Cartesian component, an absolute coordinate,
a Fourier positional feature, or a vertex index. `GeometryConditionedLinear`
adds the two elementary geometry-mediated type conversions — field-vector
$\cdot$ geometry-vector $\to$ scalar, and field-scalar $\times$
geometry-vector $\to$ vector — plus a dyad branch
$\sum C\,(v\!\cdot\!g_a)\,g_b$ that can represent anisotropic maps like
normal projection $(v\cdot n)n$, all while staying exactly linear in the
field at fixed geometry.

## Signed moment attention

The central layer, `MeshAttention`, is a **finite-rank separable signed
integral operator**. For head $h$, typed projections produce scalar and
vector query/key features $q^0_{ihr}, k^0_{jhr} \in \mathbb R$ and
$q^1_{ihrd}, k^1_{jhrd} \in \mathbb R^D$, and the pair coefficient is

$$
a_{ijh}
=\frac{1}{\sqrt{R_0+DR_1}}
\Bigl(
\sum_{r=1}^{R_0} q^0_{ihr}k^0_{jhr}
+\sum_{r=1}^{R_1} q^1_{ihr}\!\cdot\! k^1_{jhr}
\Bigr).
$$

Three deliberate absences: **no softmax** (the kernel must be signed —
double-layer kernels change sign), **no distance envelope or cutoff**
(@sec-global-flow), **no positivity or normalization** (which would break
drive linearity). The output at receiver $i$ is the quadrature-weighted sum
$o_{ihf} = \sum_j \omega_j\, a_{ijh}\, v_{jhf}$, with values retaining their
scalar/vector type.

Separability lets the sum reassociate into four typed **source moments**,

$$
M^{00}_{hrf}=\sum_j\omega_j k^0_{jhr}v^0_{jhf},\quad
M^{10}_{hrdf}=\sum_j\omega_j k^1_{jhrd}v^0_{jhf},\quad
M^{01}_{hrfe}=\sum_j\omega_j k^0_{jhr}v^1_{jhfe},\quad
M^{11}_{hrdfe}=\sum_j\omega_j k^1_{jhrd}v^1_{jhfe},
$$

built once in $O(N_s)$ and contracted at each receiver in $O(N_q)$:

$$
o^0_{ihf}=\sum_r q^0_{ihr}M^{00}_{hrf}+\sum_{r,d}q^1_{ihrd}M^{10}_{hrdf},
\qquad
o^1_{ihfe}=\sum_r q^0_{ihr}M^{01}_{hrfe}+\sum_{r,d}q^1_{ihrd}M^{11}_{hrdfe}.
$$

This is an *algebraic rearrangement* of the dense all-pairs formula, not an
approximation: every source contributes to every moment, every receiver reads
every moment. A dense `forward_reference` oracle evaluates the identical
operator in $O(N_sN_q)$ and is used for value- and gradient-equality tests. In
code, the four moments are typed views of one packed
$(R_0+DR_1)\times(F_0+DF_1)$ joint moment per head, built by a single
mesh-native `integrate_moment` call — a batched-matmul optimization measured
at 3.4–3.9$\times$ (directional; only aggregate ablation values were
retained).

The price of separability is stated up front: per head, the effective score
matrix has rank at most $R_0 + DR_1$. One layer cannot represent an arbitrary
full-rank pair kernel, a pair-specific radial function, or a singular Green
kernel. Heads and ranks are capacity knobs, not physics.

## Two streams and the linearity contract

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: >
%%|   MeshTransformer dataflow as implemented in model.py. Solid arrows are
%%|   the encode path (run once per boundary); the dashed region is the decode
%%|   path (run per query mesh, reusing the cached source moments). N-times
%%|   blocks are residual with small LayerScale initialization; the first
%%|   query cross-message initializes the field read-in with scale one.
flowchart TB
    subgraph ENC["encode(domain)  —  O(N_s)"]
        DM["DomainMesh boundaries<br/>(codim-1 cells: centroid, measure, normal)"] --> QU["merge + cell quadrature<br/>boundary-measure center c, reference length L"]
        QU --> LIFT["operator lift (TypedProjection)<br/>fields + z_j + n_j + BC one-hot"]
        LIFT --> PGB["PointwiseGeometryBlock (shared with queries)"]
        PGB --> OB["MeshOperatorBlock × L_o<br/>TypedRMSNorm → moment attention → FFN<br/>(nonlinear: geometry/operator only)"]
        DR["drive fields<br/>(boundary + global)"] --> DLIFT["GeometryConditionedLinear drive lift<br/>(linear in drive at fixed operator state)"]
        OB --> DLIFT
        DLIFT --> DB["field blocks × L_d<br/>Linear- or NonlinearZero-MeshFieldBlock"]
        OB --> DB
        DB --> MOM["source moments per query block<br/>M00, M10, M01, M11"]
        MOM --> EB["EncodedBoundary<br/>(source mesh, states, c, L, moments)"]
    end
    subgraph DEC["decode(encoded, query_mesh)  —  O(N_q)"]
        QP["query points"] --> QOP["query operator tokens<br/>(z, global operator data, association flag)"]
        QOP --> QB["query field blocks × L_q<br/>evaluate cached moments"]
        EB -.-> QB
        QB --> OUT["typed output projection<br/>(geometry-conditioned, bias-free)"]
        OUT --> PM["prediction Mesh<br/>(point_data at queries)"]
    end
```

Input fields are declared with one of two **roles**. `operator` fields
(geometry, material data, PDE coefficients) may condition the learned
operator arbitrarily; `drive` fields (the physical boundary/global data the
solution depends on) flow through a separate stream whose linearity is a
contract:

- **Operator stream.** Source tokens (declared operator fields, normalized
  centroid, normal, BC one-hot, association flag) pass through
  `MeshOperatorBlock`s: typed RMS norm, global moment self-attention,
  equivariant feed-forward, LayerScale residuals. Biases and nonlinearities
  are *allowed* here — this stream describes the operator, not the solution
  amplitude.
- **Drive stream.** In `linear` mode (`LinearMeshFieldBlock`), queries and
  keys read *only* the operator state; values are bias-free linear in the
  drive; the pointwise map is `GeometryConditionedLinear`. The complete
  drive-to-output map then satisfies $\mathcal N_\Gamma(0)=0$ and exact
  superposition at fixed geometry — the linear-PDE law of @sec-pde-theory —
  to floating point. `zero_preserving_nonlinear` mode
  (`NonlinearZeroMeshFieldBlock`) lets keys and values read the field through
  structurally multiplicative updates: zero-preservation survives,
  superposition intentionally does not.

The two modes are **different Python classes**, not flags on one class, so a
future normalization or bias added to the nonlinear block cannot silently
invalidate the linear-mode proof.

`encode` returns an `EncodedBoundary` — dimensionless source mesh, operator
and drive states, center, reference length, and the source moments for every
query block. `decode` evaluates it at any query mesh: query points never
interact, moments are reused across query chunks and across repeated decode
calls, and prediction at a point is independent of which other points are
requested — exactly the reusability structure that Green representation
(@eq-green) suggests.

## The proved limitation: an angular ceiling at order two {#sec-ceiling}

The stack carries only invariant scalars and polar vectors, and at an
ordinary interior query the *only* query-side vector is the centered position
$x$ (the query normal is zeroed; no physical global vector exists in the
benchmark). Under these assumptions, in `linear` mode with scalar output, the
decoder can produce only

$$
u(x) = c(|x|^2) + b(|x|^2)\cdot x + x^\mathsf{T} A(|x|^2)\, x,
$$

because every additional pairing of $x$ with itself reduces to powers of
$|x|^2$. On any circle centered at the model origin the angular content is
limited to Fourier orders $m \in \{0, 1, 2\}$: one monopole, two dipoles, two
quadrupoles — a boundary-to-ring operator of rank at most five. Width,
heads, separable rank, and depth add channel multiplicity and radial
structure but **cannot create an $m \ge 3$ irrep**. This is a representation
nullspace, proved in the module documentation (§6.2) and confirmed by
randomized-weight scans across width/heads/rank/depth.

The checked-in benchmark measures exactly this:

```{python}
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Pure-mode relative L2 response by boundary harmonic mode (checked-in
#|   reference_2026-07-01.json, 1,000 updates, 3 seeds, mode probes on 8
#|   geometries). The trained MeshTransformer transmits modes 0-2 and is at
#|   ~0.98-1.0 relative error (i.e., no response) for every mode >= 3 --
#|   the proved ceiling, not an optimization artifact. The dense invariant
#|   pair kernel, which forms joint source-query geometry, degrades smoothly
#|   instead.
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

reference = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "reference_2026-07-01.json"))
responses = reference["pure_mode_relative_l2"]
modes = [str(m) for m in range(9)]
mt = [responses["mesh_transformer"][m] for m in modes]
pk = [responses["invariant_pair_kernel"][m] for m in modes]

x = np.arange(len(modes))
width = 0.38
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.8, 3.4))
ax.bar(x - width / 2, mt, width, color="#2a78d6", label="MeshTransformer (135,945 p)")
ax.bar(x + width / 2, pk, width, color="#eda100", label="dense pair kernel (19,008 p)")
ax.axhline(1.0, color="#0b0b0b", lw=1.0, ls="--")
ax.text(8.42, 1.02, "no response", fontsize=8, color="#0b0b0b",
        ha="right", va="bottom")
ax.axvspan(2.5, 8.5, color="#e34948", alpha=0.06, lw=0)
ax.text(5.5, 1.14, "proved $m\\geq 3$ nullspace (linear mode, scalar output)",
        ha="center", fontsize=8.5, color="#52514e")
ax.set_xticks(x, [f"m={m}" for m in modes])
ax.set_xlabel("boundary harmonic mode (modes 1-4 occur in training)")
ax.set_ylabel("pure-mode relative $L^2$")
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.24)
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 1.0))
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Two facts sharpen the diagnosis. First, objective controls cannot fix it:
equal-interior-energy and uniform-pure-mode training leave mode-3/4 errors at
0.987/0.985 and 0.985/0.985 (checked-in ablation artifact) — you cannot
optimize your way out of a nullspace. Second, the two-by-two factorial in the
same artifact shows the bottleneck is the **source-query factorization**, not
the boundary encoder: swapping the moment decoder for a dense relative pair
decoder improves ID error by 0.34–0.39, while adding the global encoder to
the moment decoder changes it by 0.00026. Once joint source-query geometry
exists, the encoder helps (23.7% on the pair model) — a division of labor
that @sec-parametric makes precise.

## What the layer is, and is not

The honest scope, carried through the rest of the book: `MeshAttention` is an
exact, similarity-covariant, quadrature-weighted, low-order **global moment
primitive** with linear cost and a dense oracle — a rigorous building block
for boundary functionals. It is *not* a general elliptic surrogate: its
separable finite-rank kernel cannot represent the singular, domain-dependent
Poisson kernel, and its scalar query decoder has the exact $m\le2$ ceiling.
On the reference bank it reaches ID $0.458\pm0.002$ where a 19k-parameter
dense invariant pair kernel reaches $0.107\pm0.025$ — and @sec-learned-bie
shows that 3 parameters beat both, once the decoder respects the PDE. (That
comparison is available because the benchmark's PDE is known; under the
product scope it serves as the oracle the general architecture is measured
against, not as a design it can adopt.)
